doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Members of Paul Simon's band: Steve Gadd, Hugh McCracken, Richard Tee, Sanborn
summary: Toots describes the band members' playing and personalities.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: But not so… I was a little closer musically, also, because in that band with Paul Simon was Steve Kann.
[laughs] Oh, you being a drummer, or is he the drummer?

He has a foot… You know. I don’t have to… The foot… [imitating drummer] I would be a drummer, too, you know. And that’s Steve. And then there was Hugh McCracken. Fantastic guitar. He did great imitations of Elvis Presley. And he… you know, I couldn’t do. But he, yeah. And then who else? Richard Tee.

He called everybody Junior. “How ya doin’, Junior?” And he had one little sound box, you know. You see all these guy with pedals [inaudible]. He had the usual, right from the rack, you know, Fender piano, and on that a little box and a plug… [blows raspberry] and then he had a way to move. Are you familiar with his move?

[imitating] That’s him. But he was… And from the back, seeing from the was beautiful. [laughs] And playing, too. He called me... Everybody was Junior [inaudible]. “How ya doin’, Junior?” [laughs] He died, too.
[inaudible] broke his bottles that way. He broke his people.
I didn’t have to break [them?]. [laughs] Ah… I had another. See, this guy could move a building just [tapped them?]. [imitating] And some tasteful funk, you know. Whoo.
Yeah. Oh, I didn’t know that.
And the organ. Oh, yeah. That, that organ sound, everything.
Oh, well, I was going to ask you some more about the relationships. But I can understand how the Paul Simon band would have had a greater affinity with you because of the jazz.
Sanborn was in there, too. Right, right.
At the beginning of his career. That’s… I’m talking about thirty years ago, you know.
